In Slack or Teams, use an approved practice channel. Check that the app is installed and your account is linked. Ask which Devin team and project will receive the request. Start with one practice ticket and one small test. Follow the session link and check that you landed in the expected project.
The number of messages you can send depends on the plan and the length of the work.
Free accounts can create up to five projects. Check project eligibility before starting another.
Artifacts are offered on free and paid plans. Persistent storage on web and desktop is a paid-plan feature.
Usage and model access depend on how you signed in and what your account includes. Check the session status before a long job.
Web connectors are available across plans. In Team and Enterprise, an owner must first enable connectors for members.
Claude in Chrome requires a paid plan. Enterprise owners control access. Browser and computer access from web or mobile can depend on Claude Desktop.
Recurring tasks are available on paid plans. A task can run in the cloud. Local resources add a desktop dependency.
Voice sessions use the regular allowance for the account. Push-to-talk gives you control of the microphone in a noisy room.
The upload guide lists PDF, JPEG and PNG. It allows up to 20 files per chat. Check the separate rules for project knowledge.
Paid plans offer chat search. Workplace owners can control memory. Check both switches in your account.
Claude documents skills across free and paid plans. Code execution must be enabled.
The personalization guide lists account instructions and skills. Not verified — 2026-11-23: a separate Styles menu on every account.
Claude documents Research on paid plans. Check the Research control and web search access before starting.
The model determines which effort and thinking controls appear. Some models always use thinking.
Usage depends on the model, features, length of the chat and the complexity of the request. Check the limits page for the account you plan to use.
Not verified — 2026-11-23. The notebook chat guide explains selected sources and citations. It does not give a per-account notebook quota.
Google requires sign-in to use Canvas. Some sharing and AI features have extra age or account rules. Check the current guide.
Antigravity’s setup guide describes personal Free, Pro and Ultra sign-in. Check the guide that matches the account you intend to use.
Available apps vary by device, location, language and account. Work and school settings can affect which apps appear.
Google describes a gradual rollout. Incognito is excluded. Local Chrome auto browse is a desktop feature. Check the eligibility list for your account and region.
The cited Gemini Tasks guide excludes work and school accounts for this surface. Personal availability and subscription requirements vary by region.
On an iPad, open the Gemini mobile app and sign in to use Live. Google lists the Gemini web app as unavailable for Live. Updates can reach devices at different times.
Gemini accepts documents, images, audio and video. Google lists up to 10 supported files per prompt, subject to availability.
Google lists a transition starting in November 2026 for personal accounts and in 2027 for work and school accounts.
Google documents plan-dependent use and higher allowances on some accounts. A connected app is needed to include its private sources.
Google describes a gradual release and excludes work, school and supervised accounts for this feature.
Gemini in Workspace depends on your account and the app you are using. Check the Workspace feature guide for your edition.
Google documents age and account requirements for image tools. Video access depends on the offering shown for your account.
Ask needs access to a connected, indexed repo for private code questions. The public DeepWiki site offers basic questions on public repos. Full planning and session creation are in the Devin app.
The connected code host must grant access to the project. A read-only Git security profile permits reading code but prevents pushing a branch or opening a PR.
Public DeepWiki works with public GitHub projects. For a private wiki, your team must connect the repo and give Devin access to index it.
A public GitHub PR can be viewed in Devin Review without a Devin login. A private PR needs a sign-in with access. Comment triggers need the integration for that repo.
Cloud discovers SKILL.md files in connected repos. A skill saved in Customize has a personal or shared scope. As accounts move from Playbooks to Skills, existing instructions carry over.
Repo access is required before environment setup. A successful build supplies a snapshot for new sessions. Not verified (2026-11-23): a fixed number of seconds for every startup.
For enterprise sign-in with a Devin account, the assigned role needs the Use Devin CLI permission. Check your organization’s login instructions before starting.
Every visitor must sign in to Devin. With Only people with access, the creator, organization admins and people you add can open the App.
New scheduled work lives in Automations. Existing legacy schedules can still run. The editor lets you change the time zone from the browser default.
Dynamic Workflows can run in a Devin session. For enterprise accounts an admin must first enable Dynamic workflows in Enterprise Settings.
The v3 endpoint needs the organization-level UseDevinSessions permission. Each chat or ticket integration also needs its own setup and access.
A shared Outpost can serve members of the organizations it is shared with. A personal Outpost is for its owner’s sessions. Mandatory security profiles can further restrict a session’s actions.
Dispatch is a limited test for some existing Pro, Max and Ultra users. New users cannot enroll.
Paid plans include Cowork on desktop. Web and mobile access varies by plan. On Enterprise an owner must enable it.
